grades.reason: In the merged code `GET /conversations` filters with `personalScope(userId, req.workspaceId)` (conversations.js:115); the finding describes the pre-change state.
`POST /chat` now loads the conversation with `{ _id, ...personalScope(userId, req.workspaceId) }` and 404s before the stream opens (chat.js:467-471).
`UserMemory` gained `workspaceId` with an indexed default-null field and a Workspace ownerGuard (models/UserMemory.js:13,29).
`loadMemories` queries `personalScope(userId, workspaceId)` and `extractAndSaveMemories` stamps the workspace (memoryExtractor.js:137,167).

The KOL-091 Decision Log entry explicitly covers memory (UserMemory had no workspace, gains it, is written by `extractAndSaveMemories` and filtered by `loadMemories`), and a doc wording gap would not be a code defect anyway.
`deleteAccount` sweeps both models by `userId` twice (accountDeleter.js:175-176,185-190), which is exactly the pass that reaches `workspaceId: null` rows, and both tests assert it.
`sessionUserId` reads `req.session?.userId` and returns 401 when absent; there is no `req.user` or `String(id)` in this code.
`waitForMemory` does handle the timeout — `assert.ok(Date.now() < deadline, ...)` fails with a diagnostic naming the fact and the provider call count.
`String(row.workspaceId)` coerces an ObjectId to its hex string, which is what the test compares against, so the assertion is well-formed (and it fails correctly if the stamp is missing).
The null-workspace memory is verified: `result.deleted.UserMemory === 2` (accountDeleter.test.js:170) and the route-level test asserts zero `UserMemory` rows remain including the null one.

triageGrades.reason: The change's substance is an authorization-scope change — every conversation/memory lookup gains a workspace half and unreachable rows now 404 — so access-control logic is touched.
No credential, token or secret handling is added or changed; the new logging is deliberately ids-and-counts only, and conversations.js:26 holds no secret.
The change alters what gets billed where: the pre-stream 404 stops a cross-workspace turn being charged, and extraction spend follows the stamped workspace.
`accountDeleter.js` is modified — `UserMemory` joins `WORKSPACE_SCOPED_MODELS` and the user-keyed sweep switches to `+=` — so irreversible deletion code is touched.
Paid provider calls are touched: the chat route now gates them behind the scoped lookup and `memoryExtractor.js` (an outbound model call) is modified.
No version bump, deploy config, or migration — the diff deliberately ships the `$in: [id, null]` rule instead of a migration.

summary: Very poor: four of the ten findings restate the bug the diff fixes as if it were unfixed, the rest are fabricated or contradicted by the code, and the triage mislabels secrets and misses that authorization scoping is the change's whole point.
